## Skills

### AI Strategy

| Skill | Lifecycle | Editions | Reviewers | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ai-strategy:ai-maturity-assessment` | Discover, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Diagnoses an organisation's current AI maturity across strategy, people and adoption, knowledge, governance, platform and delivery capability, and value measurement, using observed evidence rather than self-scored opinion, and maps the result to a CopilotForge archetype. Use when a programme is starting, when leaders disagree about how ready they are, or when a strategy refresh needs an honest baseline. |
| `ai-strategy:ai-operating-model` | Mobilise, Scale | starter, scale, enterprise | design-authority | Designs the target operating model for AI - who decides, who builds, who supports and who owns value - choosing a central, hub-and-spoke or federated shape to suit the edition and archetype, and placing the Centre of Excellence within it. Use when AI work is spreading without clear ownership, when leaders ask how AI should be organised, or before a CoE is chartered. |
| `ai-strategy:ai-roadmap` | Mobilise, Scale, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | design-authority | Builds a prioritised, sequenced AI roadmap across the Adopt AI, Build with AI and Scale AI journeys and the lifecycle stages, showing dependencies, capacity, foundations and review points against the agreed outcomes. Use when leaders need a plan for the next twelve to twenty-four months, when initiatives compete for the same people, or when an existing roadmap has drifted from its outcomes. |
| `ai-strategy:strategic-outcomes` | Envision, Mobilise | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Turns an AI ambition into three to five measurable business outcomes, a short set of AI principles and an explicit statement of where AI will not be used, with clear expectations of the executive sponsor. Use when leaders say they want an AI strategy, when a programme has activity but no agreed outcomes, or when a sponsor needs to explain why the organisation is investing in AI. |

### Opportunity Management

| Skill | Lifecycle | Editions | Reviewers | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `opportunity-management:ai-suitability` | Envision, Deliver | starter, scale, enterprise | design-authority | Decides whether a framed business problem should be solved with AI at all, and if so which pattern fits - Copilot Chat, a Cowork task, an agent, Copilot Code, a Foundry solution or plain automation - with the reasoning recorded. Use when an idea arrives at intake, when a team has already picked a tool, or when a sponsor asks why AI is preferable to process change or training. |
| `opportunity-management:opportunity-prioritisation` | Envision, Mobilise, Scale | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Scores and balances a backlog of framed AI opportunities on value, feasibility, risk, readiness of knowledge and ownership, and strategic fit, and shapes a portfolio of quick wins and strategic bets. Admits nothing without an owner, problem, outcome, risk tier and suitability decision. Use when ideas outnumber capacity, when a steering group must choose what goes next, or when the backlog has lost its link to outcomes. |
| `opportunity-management:problem-framing` | Envision | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Turns a raw idea or tool request into a framed business problem with a named business owner, affected roles, current cost, expected outcome and baseline, and politely sends solution-first requests back to the problem. Use when an idea arrives at intake, when someone asks for an agent or Copilot feature before saying what is wrong, or when a pilot cannot say what it was meant to improve. |
| `opportunity-management:risk-classification` | Envision, Assure, Scale | starter, scale, enterprise | security-privacy, responsible-ai, evaluation-quality, design-authority | Assigns a progressive risk tier from 0 to 4 to an AI opportunity or solution by rating impact, reach, data sensitivity and autonomy, then derives the minimum governance posture and the reviewer gates it must pass, and re-classifies when scope changes. Use when an idea has a chosen pattern, when a solution is about to be shared more widely, or when someone asks which reviews a build needs. |
| `opportunity-management:scale-or-stop` | Measure, Scale, Improve | scale, enterprise | evaluation-quality, security-privacy | Makes the evidence-based decision after a pilot or first release to scale, iterate, pivot or stop, judged against the value hypothesis, adoption, quality and cost, and treats a well-evidenced stop as a success. Use when a pilot reaches its review date, when a sponsor wants to roll a solution out wider, or when a live initiative has been running for months without anyone deciding its future. |

### Copilot Adoption

| Skill | Lifecycle | Editions | Reviewers | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `copilot-adoption:adoption-measurement` | Discover, Measure, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | security-privacy | Defines how Copilot adoption is measured across usage, capability, behaviour change and business outcomes, with baselines set before launch, team or role-level reporting above a minimum group size, and feedback loops that change the programme. Use when setting adoption measures, when a sponsor asks whether Copilot is working, or when someone proposes tracking individual usage. |
| `copilot-adoption:adoption-readiness` | Discover, Mobilise | starter, scale, enterprise | security-privacy | Assesses whether an organisation or business unit is ready to adopt Microsoft Copilot across sponsorship, licences assigned versus used, IT-led technical enablement, data and permissions hygiene, approved-use guidance, support and communications, and records the gaps to close before launch. Use when licences have been bought or are about to be, before a launch date is fixed, or when early use has stalled. |
| `copilot-adoption:launch-plan` | Mobilise, Enable, Launch | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Plans a phased Copilot launch with onboarding by persona, executive and manager enablement, reinforcement through office hours and Champions, a support model and a feedback loop that keeps improving the programme. Use when readiness gaps are known and a rollout needs sequencing, when a big-bang launch is being proposed, or when a launch happened but nothing followed it. |
| `copilot-adoption:scenario-discovery` | Discover, Envision, Enable | starter, scale, enterprise | security-privacy | Segments the workforce into personas such as desk, hybrid and frontline workers, discovers role-based Copilot scenarios with business owners, prioritises them by value and frequency, and builds a scenario catalogue with prompt patterns that users can verify. Use when planning what people will actually do with Copilot, when usage is generic and shallow, or when a new team or role joins the rollout. |

### Champions

| Skill | Lifecycle | Editions | Reviewers | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `champions:capability-framework` | Enable, Measure | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Defines the three Champion capabilities - Chat, productivity and agents - each with an objective, a training option, an evidence option, verification criteria and an outcome, so training is one route rather than the gate, and maps learning sessions open to the wider business onto the journey. Use when setting what a Champion must show, when status needs to mean something, or when experienced colleagues want to skip training. |
| `champions:champion-challenges` | Enable, Deliver, Scale | scale, enterprise | security-privacy | Designs the Champion Challenge - one practical contribution after the three capabilities are verified, such as an envisioning workshop, team training, a governed business agent, a prompt library, a departmental playbook or support for the Centre of Excellence - with a safety and scope check and assessment on impact, reusability, quality and strategic alignment. Use when Champions are ready to contribute or a challenge idea needs checking. |
| `champions:champion-programme-design` | Mobilise, Enable | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Designs an evidence-led Copilot Champions programme as a progression system - purpose, the six-stage journey, operating boundaries, its place between the adoption programme and the Centre of Excellence, sponsorship, agreed time, community, tracker and self-service guidance. Use when starting or replicating a Champion network, when Champions have become an unpaid help desk, or when status means attendance. |
| `champions:evidence-assessment` | Enable, Assure | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Sets up fair, consistent assessment of Champion evidence against each capability's verification criteria and of Champion Challenges, by trained assessors who assess the evidence rather than the person, keep a restricted progress tracker, give useful feedback, handle appeals and never rank anyone. Use when submissions start arriving, when assessors disagree, when progress status is unclear or when a decision is challenged. |
| `champions:recognition-and-progression` | Measure, Scale, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Designs how Champions progress through the six-stage journey to recognised Champion, with recognition linked to demonstrated contribution, access to advanced materials, pilots and specialist pathways, renewal, a regular programme health check and programme-level measures such as milestone conversion. Use when designing Champion recognition, when status has gone stale, or when a sponsor asks whether the programme is healthy. |

### Microsoft 365 Agents

| Skill | Lifecycle | Editions | Reviewers | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `m365-agents:agent-release-readiness` | Assure, Launch, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | security-privacy, evaluation-quality, responsible-ai, design-authority | Runs the release gate for an agent, confirming owner, support route, sharing scope matched to risk tier, reviewer evidence, communications, monitoring, review date and retirement criteria, and registers the agent in the solution register. Use when an agent has passed testing and someone wants to share it, when its audience is about to widen, or when a live agent has no clear owner. |
| `m365-agents:agent-testing` | Deliver, Assure, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | evaluation-quality, security-privacy | Builds a proportionate test plan and a small evaluation set of real user questions with expected answers, covering groundedness, refusal and out-of-scope behaviour, permission trimming across different users and regression after change, against a threshold the business owner agrees. Use when an agent is ready for testing, before widening its audience, or after its instructions or knowledge change. |
| `m365-agents:agent-use-case-design` | Envision, Deliver | starter, scale, enterprise | security-privacy, design-authority | Turns an approved agent opportunity into an agent brief covering audience, purpose, scope and exclusions, instructions approach, knowledge sources, actions, the build-or-reuse decision, owner, support and success measures. Use when an idea has passed suitability as an agent, when a maker wants to start building, or when an existing agent needs its scope rewritten. |
| `m365-agents:knowledge-source-readiness` | Deliver, Assure, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | security-privacy | Assesses each knowledge source an agent will ground on for owner, currency, accuracy, permissions and oversharing, classification and review cycle, and records a ready, ready-with-conditions or not-ready verdict. Use when an agent brief names its sources, when a maker wants to add a site or library as knowledge, or when an agent starts giving outdated or surprising answers. |

### Security and Privacy

| Skill | Lifecycle | Editions | Reviewers | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `security-privacy:connector-review` | Deliver, Assure, Launch, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | security-privacy | Reviews the connectors, actions, tools, MCP servers and APIs an agent or automation uses, covering user versus maker authentication, least privilege, data policies, data leaving the tenant and confirmation for write actions, and classifies each finding as blocking or advisory with a fix. Use when an agent gains an action or tool, when a flow uses a new connector, or when a maker shares a connection. |
| `security-privacy:data-exposure-review` | Assure, Launch, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | security-privacy | Reviews what content an AI solution can reach and reveal - oversharing, permissions, sensitivity labels, the agent's sharing scope, web and public knowledge, and where outputs travel - and classifies each finding as blocking or advisory with a fix. Use when an agent or Copilot rollout reaches its security gate, when a maker adds a large knowledge source, or when sensitive content surfaces in answers. |
| `security-privacy:privacy-assessment` | Envision, Assure, Launch, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | security-privacy, responsible-ai | Assesses personal data in an AI solution for lawful basis, purpose limitation, transparency, data minimisation, retention of prompts, responses and transcripts, DPIA screening under UK GDPR and ICO guidance, and people-related uses, classifying findings as blocking or advisory. Use when an agent or AI solution processes personal data, when transcripts are kept, or when AI outputs inform decisions about people. |

### AI Centre of Excellence

| Skill | Lifecycle | Editions | Reviewers | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ai-centre-of-excellence:coe-cadence` | Mobilise, Scale, Measure, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Sets the meeting cadence and terms of reference for an AI CoE - a weekly working group, monthly steering where the sponsor decides, a quarterly strategy review and a community forum - with agendas, a decision log and sizing by edition. Use when a new CoE needs its forums set up, when meetings have become status updates that decide nothing, or when decisions are being taken in corridors and nobody can find them later. |
| `ai-centre-of-excellence:coe-charter` | Mobilise, Scale | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Drafts the charter for an AI Centre of Excellence - purpose, who owns what between the business, AI enablement and the sponsor, scope across the six pillars, decision rights, launch commitments and what the CoE is not - or the lighter terms of an AI working group. Use when leadership asks for an AI CoE, when a group has drifted into a reporting forum or request queue, or when a sponsor needs one page to agree before people are appointed. |
| `ai-centre-of-excellence:coe-governance-model` | Mobilise, Assure, Launch, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | security-privacy, responsible-ai, evaluation-quality, design-authority | Writes a proportionate AI governance framework and acceptable-use starter - five governance areas, progressive risk tiers 0 to 4 with minimum controls, an agent portfolio register with business, knowledge and technical owners, and reviewer gates - so low-risk experimentation is not blocked. Use when there is no approved AI policy, when departments build agents with no register or owner, or when governance is so heavy people work around it. |
| `ai-centre-of-excellence:coe-kpi-framework` | Measure, Scale, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Builds a KPI framework and scorecard for an AI CoE across adoption, capability, portfolio flow, quality, governance and value, each measure with a baseline, target, source and owner, rolled up into a four-quadrant sponsor dashboard at team level. Use when a sponsor asks how they will know AI is working, when reporting relies on licence counts or hours saved, or when steering needs a scorecard before its first value review. |
| `ai-centre-of-excellence:coe-operating-model` | Mobilise, Scale, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | design-authority | Designs how an AI Centre of Excellence runs - a business-owned structure with sponsor, lead, core team, four Champion roles and central AI enablement support, its shape by edition, the collaboration space, the intake-to-delivery flow and a phased launch. Use when a charter is agreed and the CoE now needs people, routes and a workable flow, or when an existing CoE has become a bottleneck. |
| `ai-centre-of-excellence:coe-raci` | Mobilise, Scale, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Builds a role-based RACI for AI work across the opportunity lifecycle, governance decisions, knowledge ownership, release and value, with exactly one Accountable per activity and the business accountable for outcomes. Use when nobody can say who approves an agent, when IT is being held to account for business benefits, or when a new CoE needs clear responsibilities before its first steering meeting. |

### Organisation Tailoring

| Skill | Lifecycle | Editions | Reviewers | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `organisation-tailoring:ai-profile-intake` | Discover | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Creates or validates an organisation profile - size, business units, regulatory context, Microsoft estate, current AI use, knowledge, governance, adoption and delivery capability - by short interview or from a file, capturing only what tailoring needs and marking unknowns. Use when someone asks for help with an AI programme and no profile exists, when a profile file is supplied, or when circumstances have changed since the last pack. |
| `organisation-tailoring:edition-and-archetype` | Discover, Envision | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Applies the CopilotForge tailoring rules to a validated organisation profile to recommend an edition (starter, scale or enterprise), an assurance overlay and a maturity archetype, citing the rule id behind each, reporting emerging signals and explaining the result to the sponsor before any pack is built. Use when a profile is ready, when a sponsor asks why they got a lighter or heavier programme, or when circumstances change. |
| `organisation-tailoring:ownership-map` | Mobilise | starter, scale, enterprise | none | Produces a role-based ownership map for an AI programme from declared roles only - the accountable role for each engaged department and each pack artefact, named owners only where the organisation has declared them, and the capability and capacity gaps to close. Use when a transformation pack needs owners, when a sponsor asks who will do this work, or when nobody can say who owns adoption, governance or agents. |
| `organisation-tailoring:transformation-pack` | Discover, Envision, Mobilise, Enable, Deliver, Assure, Launch, Measure, Scale, Improve | starter, scale, enterprise | security-privacy | Orchestrates a tailored AI transformation pack from a confirmed profile - assessment, target operating model, adoption and Champions programmes, CoE, opportunity process, agent delivery, governance, roadmap, ownership map, templates and success measures - at the depth the edition sets, and explains material changes on refresh. Use when an organisation asks for help adopting Copilot, scaling agents or setting up an AI CoE. |
